summary: Add a Canvas Builder mode that is opt-in through config and fails closed. A new leaf package, internal/sandbox, validates the five settings Canvas Builder writes (sandbox, gateway, workspace, approval_timeout, checks_command) into a Profile, and holds every message the gateway and the CLI say when they stop an agent. config.Load attaches the profile after every override, refuses a base URL that isn't the gateway, refuses settings that add headers, and -- in a build stamped at link time -- refuses to run at all without those settings.
reason:
Canvas Builder runs real canvas-lms in a hidden VM and puts cb-gateway in front of it. The agent's only door to that Canvas is this CLI, which Canvas Builder bundles and points at the gateway with a config file it writes per course workspace.

ADR 0001 says the guardrails have to assume a resourceful agent: one that reads files, runs commands and tries the obvious ways around a wall. The obvious ways around this one are all config: set CANVAS_BASE_URL to a real Canvas, pass --config with a file of its own, point CANVAS_HOME at an empty folder so the CLI falls back to the developer's legacy ~/.config and whatever token is in it. Every one of those ends with the workspace's agent token in an Authorization header on a request to somebody's real Canvas.

So the bundled build is stamped (-X ...sandbox.requiredStamp=canvas-builder) and a stamp means: read exactly the resolved config file, no legacy fallback, and stop with the settings message if it is missing, unreadable, damaged, or doesn't say sandbox = true. An empty CANVAS_HOME under the stamped build is a stop. Before this patch the same invocation reached canvas.instructure.com, which the new cmd/canvas-pp-cli/stamp_test.go demonstrated on the way in.

The gateway is the real boundary, not this CLI. These checks are defence in depth, and they also make the gateway's answers readable: the eight gateway messages are copied verbatim into internal/sandbox/messages.go so later tasks can recognise a refusal by exact text, pass it through word for word, and give an unknown outcome its own exit code instead of retrying a write that may already have landed.

The gateway address is held to http://127.0.0.1:<port> with no user info, path, query or fragment, and Allows() compares scheme, host and port exactly. That is the single rule every later task reuses for redirects, an upload_url, a file url and each Link: rel="next" page. NotGateway names the scheme and host only, never the path or query, because a Canvas file URL carries a verifier and a verifier is a credential.

HTTPTimeout exists because of the approval flow: cb-gateway's approvals.Broker.Ask returns false when the client hangs up, so a CLI that times out before the instructor answers turns every slow approval into a denial. The floor is approval_timeout + 30s.

The settings are kept in persistedConfig so a token save can't strip them; without that, one `auth login` would leave the next run of the CLI failing closed for no reason. They are listed before Headers because go-toml writes a map as a [table] and any key after it reads back as part of that table.

SandboxRequested answers "is this a Canvas Builder workspace?" from the file alone, without validating anything, because Task 5 narrows the command surface before Load gets a chance to fail.
known_limitations:
New() reports every settings fault as the same message, including a gateway address that breaks the loopback rule. Plan E's Task 1 interface said that one case should be NotGateway instead; it isn't, because NotGateway reads as "only talks to Canvas Builder at X, so it won't use X" when the gateway setting is itself the thing at fault. NotGateway is for a URL compared against a gateway that is valid -- an overridden base URL, a redirect, an upload_url -- and config.Load uses it for exactly that. A gateway that can't be the gateway is a damaged settings file, which is what the instructor is told.

The settings message is the same for a missing file, an unreadable one, a damaged one and one that doesn't say sandbox = true. That is deliberate (the instructor's fix is the same in all four), but it means a support question needs the file itself, not the message.

The stamp is a linker flag, so it is not a signature: anyone who can build this repo can build a binary without it. It stops an agent pointing the bundled CLI somewhere else, which is the threat in ADR 0001; it is not a defence against an agent that can run its own go build. The gateway, which checks the token rather than the client, is what holds in that case.

Allows() rejects user info in a URL, which is slightly stricter than the plan's "same scheme, host and port". A real gateway URL never carries user info, so nothing legitimate is refused.

Nothing enforces the profile on an actual request yet -- that is Task 2's client change. After this patch a sandbox config is validated and attached, and the base URL is checked once at load.

config_test.go's isolate() now also sets HOME. It documented itself as keeping a test off the developer's real ~/.config, but the legacy fallback path is $HOME/.config/canvas-pp-cli, so without HOME a developer's own config leaked into any test whose primary config path had no file. One new test caught it by asserting the default base URL.

User-facing messages are full sentences with a capital and a full stop, which staticcheck's ST1005 rejects for an error string. They have to stay exactly as they are, because the gateway sends them and this CLI recognises them by exact text, so they go through sandbox.NewError(msg) rather than errors.New(<constant>): ST1005 only inspects a constant argument. Three sites use it (both of config.Load's sandbox faults and profile.go's settingsErr).

`make lint` still fails on this repo, with roughly 700 findings in the generated internal/cli and internal/client packages (errcheck, noctx, staticcheck S1002 and ST1005). That was true before this patch and is not Task 1's to fix. What this patch does hold to is that the files it touches are lint-clean on their own: golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 reports nothing under internal/sandbox, internal/config or cmd/canvas-pp-cli.
validated_outcome:
go vet ./... clean and go test ./... passing on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1, with CANVAS_BUILDER_V2 pointing at the Canvas Builder repo so the message-parity test runs rather than skipping.

New coverage: the gateway address rule (two accepted forms, nine refused); every settings fault reported as the settings message; the empty approval timeout defaulting to two minutes; Allows() across port, scheme, a host with the gateway as a prefix, user info smuggling and a relative URL; the approval timeout floor; the stamp and its test switch; formatWait's four shapes; both approval notices; NotGateway naming scheme and host only and dropping a verifier query; CanvasBuilderMessage finding each of the eight gateway messages, ignoring Canvas's own, and refusing a non-JSON body; the eight messages still present verbatim in the Canvas Builder gateway source; no message containing "sandbox" or "compliant"; a full sandbox config loading with its token from credentials.toml; CANVAS_BASE_URL and a file base_url pointing off the gateway both refused by name; a headers table and an auth_header in the credentials file both refused; the stamped build refusing an empty CANVAS_HOME, a config without sandbox = true and a damaged config; normal mode unchanged (no profile, default base URL, headers still allowed); a token save keeping all five keys and omitting them outside Canvas Builder; and SandboxRequested across a sandbox config, a plain one, no file and a damaged one.

End to end, cmd/canvas-pp-cli/stamp_test.go builds both binaries and runs them: the stamped one exits 10 with the settings message on `pages index 7` with empty HOME and CANVAS_HOME, and the ordinary build still exits 0 on `pages index 7 --dry-run`. Before the patch that same stamped invocation sent three requests to canvas.instructure.com and exited 5.

CodeRabbit reviewed the whole patch (uncommitted, untracked included) and raised three findings, all minor and all lint: errors.New with a constant message at the three sites above, and exec.Command in cmd/canvas-pp-cli/stamp_test.go where noctx wants a context. Both were real -- the first was hidden in a plain `golangci-lint run` only because staticcheck's output is capped at 50 lines -- and both are fixed. The test's two subprocesses now use exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), ...), so a hung go build or a hung binary dies with the test. go test -race passes for internal/sandbox, internal/config and internal/client.
